questions: Which part of this is up to you, and which part is not?
What is the fact here, and what is the story you are adding to it?
If you had to write the next small step on a sticky note, what would it say?
Which "I have to" in this could become "I choose to" or "I won't"?
What did they actually do or say, before you decided what it meant?
What would you say to them if you knew they would listen calmly?
Which part of this relationship is up to you today?
What do you want for this person, apart from what you want from them?
What has actually happened so far, and what has only happened in your head?
If the thing you fear happened, what would you do first?
How much of this will matter to you one year from now?
What part of this can you act on today, and what can only wait?
What judgment are you making about what happened, apart from what happened?
What would a calm version of you do next?
Is the other person's behaviour up to you, or only your answer to it?
If you saw this from far above, how large would it look?
What is the smallest thing your body is asking for right now?
Which of today's "I have to" could you put down for one day?
What did you notice in your body before you started writing this?
What would rest look like if you chose it instead of falling into it?
What part of this is up to you?
Right now, what do you notice, before you explain it?
What is the fact here, and what is the story you are adding to it?
If a friend told you this, what would you ask them?

followUps: What is one small action you could take today that would be yours to take?
If you wrote this as "I choose to", what would the sentence be?
What would you do differently if you could not fail at it?
What would you want to remember about this a week from now?

quotes.text: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.work: Moral Letters to Lucilius, 13, tr. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Remember this, that very little is needed to make a happy life.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
